title: Fourth moment bound for regular functions
statement: Let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. If the function on the sign cube obtained from $f$ through the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection has every nonempty Fourier coefficient bounded in absolute value by $\varepsilon$, then the vector Fourier fourth moment of $f$ minus $(\mathbb{E}f)^4$ is at most $\varepsilon^2\operatorname{Var}(f)$, with the mean and variance taken under the uniform distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Every Fourier coefficient indexed by a nonempty coordinate subset of the induced sign-cube function has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
